status: draft until the freeze step in eval/LOOP.md writes eval/FREEZE.json

normalization.lower: same with the value axis inverted
normalization.ties: when two anchors share a value, a value meeting it gets the higher score
normalization.stretch_default: if stretch is null: if the 1.0 threshold is the metric's natural bound (100%, a full count, 0 failures) meeting it scores 100; otherwise stretch = 1.0 + (1.0 - beta) on the metric axis
normalization.ladder: level index; the level required by a milestone scores that milestone's anchor; the top level (or the level required by 1.0) scores 100
normalization.n/a: excluded from the dimension mean for that target milestone
normalization.unavailable: a metric that is not n/a for the target milestone but cannot be measured (tool or stage missing, judge uncalibrated) scores 0

dimension_score: mean of normalized metrics not excluded for the target milestone
composite: sum(weight_d * score_d) / 100; advisory - gates are binding

milestone_rule.gates: G-INT, G-PAR (P1-P10), G-SEC and G-FUZZ pass on the frozen eval set incl. held-out
milestone_rule.founder_approval: required (DECISIONS D17); the loop stops when the rule is met

human_gates.name: Novice RCT accuracy vs a placebo (Randomo-style) skin
human_gates.beta: significantly above placebo in all 3 skins (~20 novices per skin)

noise.ci95: change counts only if the 95% bootstrap CIs of old and new do not overlap
noise.mannwhitney: change counts only if > 5% and Mann-Whitney U p < 0.01 over >= 10 runs

gates.name: Eval integrity
checks: eval/MANIFEST.sha256 matches every protected file
no change under protected paths without a recorded reviewer sign-off
history.jsonl is append-only (previous lines byte-identical)
no corpus leak: compiler/ and stdlib sources contain no task id, corpus file path or expected-output line of >= 20 characters
eval/FREEZE.json eval_version equals the version being scored
gates.on_fail: iteration void; nothing is committed; loop stops and escalates

gates.name: Multilingual parity (report 05 section 2)
gates.schedule: P1-P3, P5-P9 every iteration (fast); P4 every iteration (deep); P10 nightly and at milestones
checks: P1 canonical identity: KCF SHA-256 of en/ar/franco parse of every corpus case is identical
P2 pairwise round-trip: all 6 ordered skin pairs and the 3-hop cycles give equal KCF, comments and blank lines preserved
P3 source fixpoint: print_Y(parse(print_Y(parse_X(s)))) == print_Y(parse_X(s)) byte for byte
P4 property round-trip: >=10k generated programs per run through P1-P3, 0 failures
P5 behavioural identity: identical stdout, exit code and http transcript across skins; diagnostics compared by code and line
P6 diagnostic catalog parity: every code has en/ar/franco message, help and explain page
P7 keyword-table integrity: spec section 7.4 rules over spec/keywords.json
P8 mixed-skin policy: other-skin keywords give K0201; two skin files for one module give K0301
P9 docs parity: every docs page exists x3 and its code blocks compile in its own skin
P10 LLM skin gap within the D3.skin_gap_pp threshold of the target milestone
gates.scope_rule: run/http cases: a case the parser rejects in all three skins is unsupported (it costs D1), not a parity failure; a case accepted in some skins but not others is a parity failure. compile-error cases: P1-P3 apply only when the file parses (T48 main, T49 bad, T50 homoglyph); P5 compares the set of (code, line) error diagnostics across skins, and an identical correct rejection in all three skins passes (T50 main fails before parsing by design).
gates.on_fail: the iteration's change is rejected; if already failing, the next iteration must target it

gates.name: Security hard gates
checks: 0 Vulnerable cases: MVP for CWE-89 and CWE-79; beta adds CWE-78, CWE-22, CWE-918; 1.0 covers every CWE in the security corpus
D2.trojan_source_suite passes (100% bad rejected, 100% good accepted)
D2.lexing_hazard_suite passes (100%)

gates.name: Fuzzing
checks: deep job: 15 min per fuzz target finds no new crash
milestone: D1.fuzz_crash_free_hours and D2.stdlib_parser_fuzz_hours meet the milestone threshold
gates.on_fail: crash input saved as a regression test; the iteration is rejected

gates.name: Ratchets
checks: a metric that has met its target-milestone threshold may not fall below it by more than its noise band
performance: a regression > 5% with Mann-Whitney U p < 0.01 fails
gates.on_fail: iteration rejected even if the composite rose

metrics.name: Spec clause coverage
metrics.compute: kalam-eval conformance --coverage: clauses = every numbered ### subsection of KALAM-SPEC.md sections 4-22; a clause is covered when >=1 positive and >=1 negative test under conformance/** carries `clause: <section>` front-matter. value = covered / clauses * 100.

metrics.name: Conformance pass rate (x3 skins)
metrics.compute: kalam-eval conformance --run --skins en,ar,franco: passed / total test-skin pairs * 100. A test that cannot run because a stage is missing counts as failed.

metrics.name: Corpus pass count, tier-ordered (dev + held-out, x3 skins)
metrics.compute: kalam-eval corpus --skins all --split dev, plus the sealed holdout runner (aggregates only). A task passes only if every case passes in all three skins. value = p_mvp + (p_mvp==21 ? p_beta + (p_beta==25 ? p_1_0 : 0) : 0), so a later-tier pass never substitutes for an earlier-tier failure.

metrics.name: Corpus syntax pass: MVP-tier tasks that parse, format and round-trip (dev + held-out, x3 skins)
metrics.compute: kalam-eval corpus --syntax-only --skins all --tier mvp --split dev, plus the sealed holdout runner (aggregate m1_syntax only). Scope: the 21 MVP-tier tasks T01-T15, T31-T33, T48-T50. A task counts when every case, in all three skins, is accepted by `kalam check --parse-only`, satisfies fmt(fmt(x)) == fmt(x) and kcf(fmt(x)) == kcf(x), and passes P1, P2 and P3. Parity scope rule applies: T50 main counts when all three skins give the same SEC rejection before parsing. Not scored at mvp/beta/1.0 (D1.corpus_tier_pass supersedes it); gating only in milestone tier M1.

metrics.name: Differential execution (scope with 0 mismatches)
metrics.compute: kalam-eval differential: run corpus + generated programs on each backend pair and compare stdout/stderr/exit. value = highest level whose scope had 0 mismatches.
levels: MVP: JS(node) vs reference interpreter on the corpus + 1k generated programs
beta: + JS(browser, Playwright) and 10k generated programs per iteration
1.0: + WASM/C backend when present and 1M generated programs per week

metrics.name: Compiler fuzzing, crash-free hours

metrics.name: Property suites pass (fmt idempotence, round-trip, stdlib laws)
metrics.compute: cargo test -p kalam-props --release; value = all properties pass on >=10k cases each.

metrics.name: Compiler line coverage
metrics.compute: cargo llvm-cov --workspace --json over the full test run; value = lines.percent.

metrics.name: Compiler branch coverage
metrics.compute: cargo llvm-cov --workspace --branch --json; value = branches.percent.

metrics.name: Secure-by-default rate (inverted OWASP/Juliet corpus)
metrics.compute: kalam-eval seccorpus: ~150 'bad' cases x 3 skins (CWE-89/78/94/79/22/918/502/601/798/862/352/1333; T48-T50 included). Each case is classified Impossible (typed compile error), Escaped (compiles only via unsafe.*/extern/.expose()), Mitigated (compiles; exploit payload neutralized at runtime) or Vulnerable (payload succeeds or case not decidable). value = (I+E+M)/total*100.

metrics.name: Share of bad cases that are Impossible
metrics.compute: same run as D2.secure_by_default_rate; value = Impossible/total*100.

metrics.name: Good-twin usability
metrics.compute: kalam-eval seccorpus --good: the secure twin of each case compiles and passes its tests.

metrics.name: Trojan Source suite (~60 cases incl. T50)
metrics.compute: kalam-eval trojan: every bad case rejected with the expected SEC code naming the code point; every good case (escaped controls, legitimate Arabic text, emoji ZWJ) accepted.

metrics.name: Arabic/Franco lexing hazard suite
metrics.compute: kalam-eval lexhaz: normalization, alef/hamza and ى/ي folding in keywords, tatweel/harakat, Persian/Urdu letters ی ک ە ھ ۀ folded to their Arabic equivalents in identifiers and keywords (DECISIONS D19: fold, not reject) with a lookalike collision after folding still a compile error (SEC0104; it needs name resolution, so those cases count from tier M2), Arabic-Indic and Persian digits, U+066B/U+066C, Franco digit-letter boundaries (3ala, 7asab, 2ktb) with did_you_mean.

metrics.compute: kalam audit --json over all dev corpus programs (en skin): count(unsafe.* + extern + .expose()) / KLOC. Counted on the AST, never by grep (spec P10).
